requirements.title: C external-linkage variables may interoperate with BIND module variables or common blocks
requirements.source: S18.9.1 p1.c-global-interoperation-permitted; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF544.
requirements.definition: A C variable with external linkage may interoperate with a common block or with a variable declared in a module scope.

pending.c-external-variable-interoperates-with-b: Mixed C plan defines global int c_extern with value 101; After guarding C_INT > 0 before any C_INT-kind declaration, Fortran declares integer(c_int), bind(C, name="c_extern") :: f_extern in a module, reads 101, writes 103, and C reads back 103 through a helper function.

Mixed C plan defines struct global com with float members r=1.25 and s=-2.5; After guarding C_FLOAT > 0 before any C_FLOAT-kind declaration, Fortran declares matching real(c_float) common /com/ r, s with BIND(C), reads both exact binary values, writes 3.5 and 4.5, and C reads the updated members.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Mixed Fortran/C plans use the suite C interop harness with separate C and Fortran sources. They guard every ISO_C_BINDING kind constant with k > 0 before using it as a kind and observe only portable properties fixed by Clause 18: exact integer or exactly representable real sentinel values, successful linkage through required binding labels, Fortran ALLOCATED or ASSOCIATED status after CFI calls, and required diagnostics for numbered constraints. Program obligations on C descriptors, object lifetimes, setjmp/longjmp, signal handling, floating-point status, and asynchronous communication are not treated as required diagnostics unless a numbered constraint owns the rejection.

requirements.title: Interoperating common blocks and module variables have the BIND attribute
requirements.source: S18.9.1 p1.bind-required; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF544.
requirements.definition: The common block or module variable that interoperates with a C external-linkage variable shall be specified to have the BIND attribute.

requirements.title: Only one Fortran variable may be associated with a particular C external variable
requirements.source: S18.9.1 p2.one-fortran-variable-per-c-variable; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF544.
requirements.definition: Across all Fortran program units of a program, at most one variable associated with a particular C variable whose name has external linkage is permitted.

requirements.title: A variable is initially defined by no more than one processor
requirements.source: S18.9.1 p2.one-initial-defining-processor; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF544.

requirements.title: BIND common blocks use the same binding label in every declaring scoping unit
requirements.source: S18.9.1 p3.common-same-binding-label; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF544.
requirements.definition: A common block specified in a BIND statement shall use a BIND statement with the same binding label in each scoping unit where it is declared.

requirements.title: C structure variables interoperate with corresponding BIND common-block members
requirements.source: S18.9.1 p3.common-structure-correspondence; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF544.
requirements.definition: A C external-linkage variable of structure type interoperates with a BIND common block whose member variables are interoperable with corresponding structure components.

requirements.source: S18.9.1 p4; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF544.

Permission for cross-language association of C external variables with Fortran BIND entities.
Common-block label consistency and two C/common correspondence alternatives are split.
Permission for a BIND Fortran entity without a C counterpart.
Example only; the normative label and interoperation rules are catalogued from p1-p4 and 18.9.2.

review_rationale: Source registration for 18.6-18.10.4: restrictions on C descriptors and lifetimes, interoperation with C global variables and binding labels, and interoperation with C functions (batch245). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; cross-language calls, descriptors and binding labels are planned as mixed Fortran/C programs with exact results, and program-side restrictions carry no oracle. C1807 had no existing tests. Source accounting only.
